sentences.text: Today’s lesson covers the two situations you’ll face most in a powerboat, plus the duties that go with them.
We start with the simplest: head-on.
Rule fourteen applies when two power-driven vessels meet on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses, with a risk of collision.
Each alters course to starboard, so they pass port to port.
In a head-on situation, there’s no stand-on vessel.
How do you know you’re head-on?
You see the other vessel ahead, or nearly ahead.
At night, you’d see her masthead lights in a line, or nearly in a line, or both of her sidelights at once.
Red and green together, coming at you, means turn right.
And if you’re in any doubt whether it’s a head-on situation, assume that it is, and act accordingly.
Here’s a memory hook: when you meet, go right, and show her your red.
